chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:

I asked him about a man who missed one rak'ah with the Imam during the days of Tashriq. He said: 'He completes his prayer, then says Takbir.' I asked him about the Takbir during the days of Tashriq: after how many prayers? He said: 'As many as you wish, for it is not fixed in time, meaning in the speech (of the prayer).'

key_terms.أَيَّامَ التَّشْرِيقِ: Days of Tashriq (the 11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for completing a missed prayer and performing Takbir during the days of Tashriq?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the distinction is made between the obligatory post-prayer Takbir of Eid and the voluntary, non-fixed remembrance (dhikr) associated with the Days of Tashriq. The Imam clarifies that for one who joins late, the subsequent Takbir is not bound by a specific numerical limit, reflecting the scholarly view that the extended Takbir during Tashriq is a recommended sunnah rather than a strictly timed fard, allowing flexibility in its performance after the obligatory prayer.
